configs.title: Dengue time tree with one partition per gene (dengue/20).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-timetree.schema.json

# Dengue time tree with one partition per gene (dengue/20).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime timetree --config data/dengue/20/timetree-gene-partitions.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/dengue/20/timetree-gene-partitions
#
# The genes of the dengue genome evolve at different rates, and the untranslated
# regions at both ends have constraints of their own. The setting
# `partition_by: genes` makes one partition per CDS of `annotation.gff3` and one
# partition `noncoding` of the other sites. The CDS are those of the DENV2
# reference NC_001474 in nextstrain/dengue@b31c2b5
# (phylogenetic/defaults/denv2/reference.gb), and the alignment columns are the
# positions of that reference. The prM CDS `M` contains `pr`, so `pr` gets no
# partition of its own. All partitions share the tree and the branch lengths;
# each partition fits its own relative rate (`partition_rates: estimate`), and
# the partitions share one set of exchange rates and frequencies (the default of
# the genes scheme). The rates of the partitions are in the model output.
# Fitting relative rates requires re-estimating branch lengths. This subset
# has all input branches below the 0.1 substitutions-per-site cutoff for
# marginal branch-length estimation.
#
# The clock rate is estimated from the data; the Nextstrain denv2 genome build
# fixes it at 0.00078 (phylogenetic/defaults/config_dengue.yaml line 36).
# `coalescent: opt` fits a constant coalescent time scale, as the build does, and
# `seed` makes the random order of the polytomy resolution reproducible.

tree: "tree.nwk"
metadata: "metadata.tsv"
metadata_id_columns:
  - "genbank_accession"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"
annotation:
  - "annotation.gff3"

partition_by: "genes"
partition_rates: "estimate"
branch_length_mode: "marginal"
coalescent: "opt"
seed: 42

configs.title: Dengue time tree with a simpler substitution model for the UTRs than for the coding region (dengue/20).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-timetree.schema.json

# Dengue time tree with a simpler substitution model for the UTRs than for the coding region (dengue/20).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime timetree --config data/dengue/20/timetree-partition-models.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/dengue/20/timetree-partition-models
#
# Each `partition` entry names its sites and its own substitution model. The coding
# region, sites 97-10269 of the DENV2 reference NC_001474 (the CDS of
# `annotation.gff3`), fits GTR (`model` left out means `infer`). The entry `utr`
# names no sites, so it takes the remaining sites, the 5' and 3' UTRs, and uses
# JC69, which has no parameters besides the relative rate of the partition. On
# this tree of 20 genomes the 550 UTR sites carry about 130 of about 4500 expected
# substitutions, so JC69 spends none of them on the five exchange rates and three
# base frequencies of GTR. Named models can also take parameters: `model: "hky85"`
# with `model_params: ["kappa=4"]`. The clock rate is estimated from the data;
# `coalescent: opt` fits a constant coalescent time scale, and `seed` makes the
# random order of the polytomy resolution reproducible.

tree: "tree.nwk"
metadata: "metadata.tsv"
metadata_id_columns:
  - "genbank_accession"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

partition:
  - name: "coding"
    sites: ["97-10269"]
  - name: "utr"
    model: "jc69"
partition_rates: "estimate"
coalescent: "opt"
seed: 42

#   treetime optimize --config data/flu/h3n2/20/optimize-reroot-min-dev.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/flu/h3n2/20/optimize-reroot-min-dev
#
# `optimize` re-estimates every branch length under the substitution model and
# (here) reroots to minimize root-to-tip divergence variance. This is the
# date-free step that replaces `augur refine` in a Nextstrain build.

tree: "tree.nwk"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

# Per-edge optimizer: Brent's method in sqrt(t) space (the default, matches v0).

# Reroot by minimizing root-to-tip divergence variance (a date-free method).

configs.title: Time-scaled tree with a fixed clock rate and date confidence intervals (flu/h3n2/200).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-timetree.schema.json

# Time-scaled tree with a fixed clock rate and date confidence intervals (flu/h3n2/200).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime timetree --config data/flu/h3n2/200/timetree-fixed-clock.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/flu/h3n2/200/timetree-fixed-clock
#
# `timetree` turns divergence into calendar time. Fixing the clock rate (`clock_rate`)
# skips rate estimation and is common for well-characterized pathogens like seasonal
# influenza. `confidence` adds date confidence intervals, which need a rate
# uncertainty (`clock_std_dev`) when the rate is fixed; `coalescent: opt` fits a
# constant coalescent time scale analytically. The rate and its uncertainty are those
# of the Nextstrain h3n2 NA builds.

tree: "tree.nwk"
metadata: "metadata.tsv"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

clock_rate: 0.00267
clock_std_dev: 0.000534
confidence: true
coalescent: "opt"
max_iter: 3

# A fixed seed makes the random steps of the run, such as polytomy resolution, repeat
# exactly.
seed: 42

# The default outputs: with `confidence`, the node dates table holds the 90%
# intervals.
output_selection:
  - "nwk"
  - "nexus"
  - "auspice"
  - "node-data"
  - "model"
  - "sequences"
  - "clock-model"
  - "coalescent"
  - "dates"

configs.title: Branch lengths with discrete gamma rate variation across sites (sc2/2844).

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-optimize.schema.json

# Branch lengths with discrete gamma rate variation across sites (sc2/2844).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime optimize --config data/sc2/2844/optimize-gamma.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/sc2/2844/optimize-gamma
#
# Most sites of a SARS-CoV-2 genome never change on a tree of a few years, while a
# few sites change many times. `gamma_categories: 4` lets each site evolve in one of
# four rate categories of equal probability, whose rates follow a gamma distribution
# with a fitted shape (`gamma.shape` in the model output; a shape below 1 means that
# most sites are slow and a few fast). Four categories are the default of the `+G`
# model of IQ-TREE, whose GTR+G fit gave the branch lengths of `tree.nwk` (see
# `README.md`). The run takes about ten minutes, many times longer than optimize
# without rate variation (kb/decisions/discrete-gamma-rate-variation.md).

tree: "tree.nwk"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

gamma_categories: 4

configs.title: Branch lengths with one partition per SARS-CoV-2 gene (sc2/2844).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-optimize.schema.json

# Branch lengths with one partition per SARS-CoV-2 gene (sc2/2844).

#   treetime optimize --config data/sc2/2844/optimize-gene-partitions.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/sc2/2844/optimize-gene-partitions
#
# The genes of SARS-CoV-2 evolve at different speeds: the spike gene S, for example,
# is under selection by the immune response. `partition_by: genes` makes one partition
# for each CDS of the Wuhan-Hu-1 annotation and one for the noncoding sites. The
# partitions share the branch lengths and, by default for this scheme, one set of
# exchange rates and equilibrium frequencies, because the genes of one genome share
# the mutation process; each partition fits its own relative rate. The model output
# lists the rate of each gene (`mu`): on this tree ORF1b, which codes for the
# polymerase, evolves slowest, and the noncoding sites, which include the genome ends
# that are hard to sequence, fastest. A site in two CDSs belongs to the longer CDS, so
# ORF9b, which lies inside N, gets no partition, and the run warns about it.

tree: "tree.nwk"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"
annotation:
  - "annotation.gff3"

partition_by: "genes"

configs.title: Branch lengths with the sites grouped by how often they change (sc2/2844).
configs.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neherlab/treetime/rust/packages/schemas/input-config-optimize.schema.json

# Branch lengths with the sites grouped by how often they change (sc2/2844).
#
# Run from any folder; relative paths in this file resolve from its folder, and
# `--output-all` chooses the output folder. From the repository root:
#   treetime optimize --config data/sc2/2844/optimize-rate-categories.yaml --output-all tmp/examples/sc2/2844/optimize-rate-categories
#
# `partition_by: rate-categories` counts, for each site, the branches of the input
# tree with a Fitch parsimony change at that site, and puts the sites into three
# partitions: `slow` (no change), `medium` (one change) and `fast` (two or more
# changes). The partitions share the exchange rates and base frequencies and fit one
# relative rate each (kb/decisions/multi-alignment-partitions.md). Like
# `optimize-gamma.yaml`, this lets a few fast sites carry most substitutions, and
# the run takes about a fifth of the time of the gamma example. The buckets come
# from the same data and tree as the fit, so their rates are not independent
# estimates: in a simulation with known site rates in that decision file, the
# buckets made the tree 0.8 to 1.4 % too long. On this dataset the tree comes out
# shorter than without partitions, while gamma makes it longer, so the two methods
# are not interchangeable.

tree: "tree.nwk"
alignment:
  - "aln.fasta.xz"

partition_by: "rate-categories"

# The input is the hand-made graph of README.md: 10 samples, three segments, two

#
# `mugration` treats a discrete metadata column (here `country`) like a
